prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for hurricane‑rated replacements in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and whether you need a certified hurricane‑rated system (Miami‑Dade NOA, high‑wind shingles, TPO/PVC for low slope, etc.). I can help you find the best match, but first here’s how to identify one and a few ways to get a vetted short list.

What to require from any contractor
- Valid Florida license and local registration (check Florida DBPR and city/county records).  
- Experience with Miami‑Dade County building code and Miami‑Dade Product Control NOA (Notice of Acceptance) installations for the materials they use.  
- Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred) for warranty support.  
- Written, dual warranties: manufacturer warranty + contractor workmanship warranty (check length and transferability).  
- Proof of insurance (general liability + worker’s comp) and ability to pull permits.  
- Experience handling insurance claims, if you’ll be using insurance money.  
- References and photos of recent hurricane‑rated installations locally.  
- Clear written scope, itemized estimate, payment schedule, timeline, and permit/inspection process.

Red flags to avoid
- Only cash deals, requests for large upfront payment without lien releases.  
- No local references, no permits, or reluctance to provide license numbers.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or to waive required inspections.

Where to find and vet contractors
- Florida DBPR license lookup: confirm contractor license and disciplinary history.  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control NOA database: confirm the specific roofing system the contractor plans to use is approved.  
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) to find certified contractors near you.  
- Local review sites: BBB, Google Reviews, Angi/HomeAdvisor — read recent reviews and responses.  
- Ask neighbors, HOA, or local builders for referrals after storms.

Questions to ask when getting bids
- “Provide your Florida license number and proof of insurance.”  
- “Is the roofing system you recommend Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved? Give the NOA number.”  
- “Are you a certified installer for the manufacturer? Show certification.”  
- “What warranties come with this project (manufacturer + workmanship)? Are they transferable?”  
- “Who will pull permits and coordinate inspections?”  
- “Can you provide 3 local references of completed hurricane‑rated roof replacements?”

If you want, I can:
- Look up top‑rated contractors near you (give me a ZIP code or neighborhood).  
- Vet up to 3 contractors for licenses, NOA compliance and certifications if you paste their names/quotes.

Tell me your ZIP code or share any companies you’re considering and I’ll pull a short, vetted list.
